connect.pos: Noun (in place of が or を)

examples.ja: この歌は人気があって、小さい子ども{まで}歌っています。
examples.en: This song is so popular that even small children sing it.

examples.ja: [簡単|かんたん]な漢字をまちがえて、妹に{まで}[笑|わら]われました。
examples.en: I got an easy kanji wrong and was laughed at even by my little sister.

watch.note: まで takes the place of が and を. Other particles such as に stay in front of it: 妹にまで.
watch.bad: その話は、大学の先生がまで知っています。
watch.good: その話は、大学の先生まで知っています。

connect.pos: Noun (in place of が or を)

examples.ja: [息子|むすこ]はいつも肉{ばかり}食べて、野菜を食べません。
examples.en: My son always eats nothing but meat and doesn't eat vegetables.

examples.ja: せっかくの旅行だったのに、雨{ばかりの}一週間でした。
examples.en: It was a trip I had looked forward to, but it rained all week.

watch.note: ばかり means a lot of one kind, or the same thing again and again. For one single person or thing, use だけ.
watch.bad: このクラスで日本人は私ばかりです。
watch.good: このクラスで日本人は私だけです。

compare.intro: まで adds a surprising extra, ばかり complains that there is too much of one thing, and だけ simply says there is nothing else.

forms.tag: そこまで · even, as far as
forms.ja: 社長{まで}[会議|かいぎ]に[遅|おく]れてきました。
forms.en: Even the company president came late to the meeting.

forms.tag: 同じものが多い · nothing but
forms.ja: [会議|かいぎ]では、[部長|ぶちょう]{ばかり}話していました。
forms.en: In the meeting, the department head did all the talking.

forms.ja: [会議|かいぎ]に来たのは、田中さん{だけ}でした。
forms.en: Ms Tanaka was the only one who came to the meeting.

check.label: Even, nothing but, or only?
check.q: パーティーで作った料理がみんなにほめられて、ふだん何も言わない父（　　）「おいしい」と言ってくれました。
why: ばかり needs a lot of one thing or the same thing again and again. Here one person says it once.
だけ would mean only father praised the food, but みんなにほめられて says everyone did.
Everyone praised it, and even quiet father said it was good: 父まで.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: かぜがひどくなって、^[熱|ねつ]が出て^、のど（　　）[痛|いた]くなってきました。
why: しか needs a negative verb after it (のどしか痛くない). Here the verb is positive.
ほど needs a comparison or a degree (のどが痛いほど…). のどほど痛くなってきた makes no sense.
こそ picks out one thing as the very one. Here the throat is added to the fever, not picked out.
A fever, and on top of that even a sore throat: のどまで.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^同じミス^（　　）して、[課長|かちょう]に注意されてしまいました。
why: The same mistake again and again, and a scolding: 同じミスばかり.
しか needs a negative verb after it (ミスしかしない). Here the verb is positive.
ほど needs a comparison or a degree. ミスほどして makes no sense.
こそ picks out one thing as the very one, often with praise or a strong point. It does not fit a mistake made over and over.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: [引っ越|ひっこ]しのとき、友だちだけでなく、となりの人（　　）^[手伝|てつだ]ってもらいました^。
why: までに gives a deadline, which does not fit a person.
もらう takes に for the helper, and に stays in front of まで: となりの人にまで.
ばかり would mean only the neighbour helped, but 友だちだけでなく says friends helped too. に is also missing.
まで takes the place of を. をまで is never used.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: テレビをつけても、暗いニュース（　　）で、^いやになります^。
why: まで adds one surprising extra to other things, but nothing else is mentioned here, and 暗いニュースまでで makes no sense.
さえで is not used. さえ needs a negative or ば after it (ニュースさえなければ).
Nothing but gloomy news, and a complaint: 暗いニュースばかりで.
しか needs a negative verb after it (ニュースしかない). しかで is not used.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before: 近所のパン屋が[閉|し]まるという
drill.hint: という needs a noun right after it. まで follows the particle に.
drill.full: 近所のパン屋が[閉|し]まるといううわさはとなりの町に{まで}広がっていました。
drill.explain: という describes うわさ, so うわさは comes first. となりの describes 町, and まで follows に: the rumour that the local bakery is closing had spread even to the next town.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: ばかり follows a noun. Which tiles together describe that noun?
drill.full: このデパートは[値段|ねだん]が高いもの{ばかりで}、なかなか買えません。
drill.explain: 値段が高い describes もの, and ばかりで follows the noun and gives the reason: this department store has nothing but expensive things, so I can hardly buy anything.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: このゲームは本当に難しくて、ゲームが得意な兄（　　）途中でやめてしまった。
exam.explain: The game is so hard that even my brother, who is good at games, gave up: 兄までも. しか needs a negative verb after it. こそ picks out one thing as the very one, which does not fit here. ばかり needs a lot of one thing or the same thing again and again, but here one person gives up once.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: このあたりは、古い家（　　）静かな町です。
exam.explain: Before a noun, ばかりの: a quiet town with nothing but old houses. さえ and までに cannot join 古い家 to 静かな町. だけで needs a verb after it (古い家だけでできている); it cannot describe the noun 町 directly.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.before: この映画は話題になっていて、ふだん
exam.after: 見に行っているそうです。
exam.full: この映画は話題になっていて、ふだん映画を{見ない}人まで見に行っているそうです。
exam.explain: 映画を, 見ない, 人, まで. 映画を見ない describes 人, and まで follows the noun: the film is talked about so much that even people who don't usually watch films are going to see it.

scene.intro: You are standing in front of the menu board in your company cafeteria. Tap each word on it.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: このランチは数量_げんてい_なので、早めに来てください。
check.explain: げんてい is 限定: 限 means limit (限る), and 定 means fixed (予定). 現 is "now" as in 現在, 減 is "decrease" as in 減る, and 低 is "low" as in 低い. None of them makes a word with this meaning.

skill.ask: What does the notice say about the new set meal?
skill.passage: 最近、社員食堂では、カレーやラーメンなど、量が多くてあぶらの多いメニューばかり選ぶ人が目立ちます。体重が気になっている人もいるでしょう。そこで、来月から、野菜をたっぷり使った「健康定食」を始めます。^毎日二十食の数量限定^で、季節の野菜のほか、デザートに果物までつきます。^値段はほかの定食と同じ五百円^です。^人気が出ると売り切れることもありますので、食券はお昼前に買っておくと安心です^。また、どの定食にも、^野菜の小皿を百円で追加できます^。
skill.strategy: Check each option against the details in the notice: how many, how much, and what costs extra.

item.q: 「健康定食」について、このお知らせからわかることは何か。
options: ほかの定食より百円高い。
食べたい人は、毎日だれでも食べられる。
食券は昼になる前に買っておいたほうがいい。
野菜の小皿が無料でつく。
short: 毎日だれでも食べられる
item.explain: The notice says the meal may sell out, so it is safer to buy the ticket before noon: 食券はお昼前に買っておくと安心です.
why: The price is the same as the other set meals, 500 yen.
Only twenty are made each day (数量限定), so not everyone can have it.
The small vegetable dish costs 100 yen extra, and it can be added to any set meal.
